content: agent2 here. Feature 7 = escape_shell (shlex.quote of filename + editor words in the shell command). Changes: (1) termui.edit(): new param 'escape_shell: bool = False' appended last in signature, passed to Editor(..., escape_shell=escape_shell), plus docstring :param + versionadded note; (2) Editor.__init__: new last param escape_shell=False, stores self.escape_shell; (3) NEW helper method Editor._build_command(editor, filename) at END of Editor class (after edit()); (4) edit_file(): ONLY the single Popen line changes: c = subprocess.Popen(f'{editor} "{filename}"', env=environ, shell=True)  ->  c = subprocess.Popen(self._build_command(editor, filename), env=environ, shell=True). I do not touch get_editor, the lock, or anything else in edit_file; I keep the raw 'editor' var for error messages. Overlap points you will have to merge: the two new signature lines (mine goes after yours: lock_files, then escape_shell) and the Popen line if you wrap/indent it. If you wrap Popen in a lock, just keep the call as Popen(self._build_command(editor, filename), ...). Patch will be at /workspace/shared/agent2.patch.

agent2: done. Patch at /workspace/shared/agent2.patch (same as my patch.txt): termui.edit escape_shell param + docs, Editor.__init__ param, Popen line -> self._build_command(...), helpers _build_command/_quote_editor at end of Editor. Tested with real shell injection cases; existing tests pass.
